topic_summary: Analysis of the Bitcoin whitepaper's consensus rules as a contested kernel, examining competing interpretations of protocol immutability between Sound Money Maximalists (strict originalism, monetary rules as fixed) and Utility Governance advocates (evolutionary protocol via soft forks and layers). The dispute centers on whether the 2008 whitepaper establishes immutable monetary policy or a flexible substrate for iterative improvement.

key_entities: Bitcoin Whitepaper (2008 Satoshi Nakamoto document; founding text)
Sound Money Maximalists (originalist interpretation; protocol ossification)
Utility Governance Advocates (evolutionary interpretation; layer-2 scaling)
21 Million Supply Cap (fixed issuance schedule; monetary policy)
key_tensions: Protocol immutability vs protocol evolution (ossification vs soft fork governance)
Store-of-value function vs payment-system function (digital gold vs peer-to-peer cash)

axes.selection_reason: Third structural position attempting reconciliation; tests coherence of hybrid framework

omegas.description: Does Satoshi's forum commentary (2009-2010) constitute binding interpretive authority? If yes, maximalist reading gains ground (block size limit discussions). If no, utility reading claims original flexibility.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) + kernel authority grounding

omegas.description: The 2013 chain split and 2017 SegWit2x rejection established de facto immutability norms. Are these kernel stabilizations or contingent political outcomes?
If mining becomes sufficiently concentrated, does PoW cease to be a Mountain (physics of hash rate) and become a Snare (cartel enforcement)? Deferred axis mining_centralization_drift surfaces this.
Do Lightning Network and sidechains constitute readings of the kernel (utility_reading) or evasions of kernel constraints? If substitution, pragmatic_synthesis collapses.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel structure confirmed: three readings emit structurally distinct constraints with different beneficiary/victim sets. Maximalist reading treats monetary rules as absolute (high ε); utility reading treats them as negotiable via soft consensus (mod ε); pragmatic synthesis attempts hybrid (low ε scaffold). All three coexist as live social positions.

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The Bitcoin whitepaper's specification of proof-of-work longest-chain consensus and 21 million supply cap as stabilized protocol commitments
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Miner signaling + node operator enforcement + developer consensus (no single interpreter; distributed legitimacy)

readings.commitment: Whitepaper establishes immutable monetary policy; any change violates founding covenant
readings.expected_structural_delta: High extractiveness against protocol changes; beneficiaries are holders/early adopters; victims are scalability/innovation layers

readings.commitment: Whitepaper establishes minimum viable consensus mechanism enabling iterative improvement
readings.expected_structural_delta: Moderate extractiveness; soft forks and layer-2 protocols as legitimate evolution; beneficiaries are adopters/builders; victims are monetary ossification guarantees

readings.commitment: Base layer monetary rules are immutable; upper layers permit innovation without kernel violation
readings.expected_structural_delta: Low extractiveness scaffold; attempts to satisfy both camps by segregating immutability (base) from flexibility (layers); victim is ideological coherence

axiom_contradictions.basis: Maximalist axiom (protocol immutability as sacred) is mutually exclusive with utility axiom (protocol adaptability as necessary). No single framework can hold both 'changes are violations' and 'changes are improvements' simultaneously for the same protocol layer.
